name: Johnny B Rhythm
memo: Chuck Berry - Johnny B. Goode: rhythm and solos. Clean-edge CRUNCH, Fender-style amp with a hollowbody Gibson, slapback echo.

band.style_feel: fast driving shuffle-ish rock and roll, straight-ahead backbeat on 2 and 4, boogie bass pattern
parts: Part A: intro lick and 12-bar verse - steady backbeat, boogie feel
Part B: chorus ("Go, go, Johnny go") - same 12-bar form, full band
Part C: solo - full band, driving
band.tips: Sources give about 168-170 BPM (the recording drifts a little); the Trio+ may need a Rock style with a fast straight feel. Play the intro lick, then 2 bars of steady double-stop boogie before it starts learning.

whammy.tuning: Standard (E A D G B E)
how: Tune your guitar to standard (E A D G B E).
whammy.tips: The recording is in standard tuning and no pitch effect is documented, so the pedal is not needed.

guitar.position: bridge pickup, volume full, tone knob around 7
guitar.tone_notes: Sources say Berry used either the 1957 ES-350T with PAF humbuckers or the 1956 ES-350TN with P-90s; the exact guitar on the session is not confirmed. A semi-hollow or humbucker guitar fits best; with single-coils roll back treble a little.
